questions.question: 25 cards are numbered from 1 to 25. One card is drawn at random. The probability that the number drawn on the card is not a multiple of 3, is
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Number of multiples of 3 up to 25 = 25 ÷ 3 ≈ 8 (taking the integer part).

Number of cards that are NOT multiples of 3 = 25 − 8 = 17.

Required Probability = Favorable Outcomes ÷ Total Outcomes = 17/25.

**∴ The correct answer is 17/25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total number of cards = 25 (numbered 1 to 25)

**Formula Used:**

Probability P(E) = Number of favorable outcomes ÷ Total number of possible outcomes

P(Not E) = 1 − P(E)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6f3f61e48105aafa55ea4f9fd187fa6101e060b8b589969edaebb7d38520e3f2.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sample space S = {1, 2, 3, ..., 25}

⇒ Total possible outcomes, n(S) = 25

⇒ Let E be the event of drawing a multiple of 3.

⇒ E = {3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 24}

⇒ Number of favorable outcomes for E, n(E) = 8

⇒ Probability of drawing a multiple of 3, P(E) = n(E) ÷ n(S) = 8/25

⇒ Probability of NOT drawing a multiple of 3 = 1 − P(E)

⇒ 1 − 8/25 = (25 − 8) / 25 = 17/25

**∴ The correct answer is 17/25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Complementary Events

The sum of the probabilities of an event happening and not happening is always equal to 1. Formula: P(A) + P(A') = 1.

Finding Multiples in a Range

To find the number of multiples of a number 'k' from 1 to 'N', you simply take the greatest integer less than or equal to N ÷ k.

Mutually Exclusive Events

Two events are mutually exclusive if they cannot happen at the same time. The probability of either event occurring is the sum of their individual probabilities: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B).

questions.question: The base of a right prism is a triangle whose sides are 8 cm, 15 cm and 17 cm, and its lateral surface area is 480 cm². What is the volume (in cm³) of the prism?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sides 8, 15, 17 form a right-angled triangle (8² + 15² = 17²).

Base Area = 1/2 × 8 × 15 = 60 cm².

Base Perimeter = 8 + 15 + 17 = 40 cm.

Height of Prism = Lateral Surface Area ÷ Perimeter = 480 ÷ 40 = 12 cm.

Volume = Base Area × Height = 60 × 12 = 720 cm³.

**∴ The correct answer is 720 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Base sides = 8 cm, 15 cm, 17 cm

Lateral Surface Area (LSA) = 480 cm²

**Formula Used:**

LSA of Prism = Perimeter of base × Height

Volume of Prism = Area of base × Height

Area of right triangle = 1/2 × Base × Perpendicular

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/546911280e55ef9f06762f18f0439944676deb3a4e47373a1df77b32e98f2789.png] 

Checking if base is a right triangle:

⇒ 8² + 15² = 64 + 225 = 289

⇒ 17² = 289

⇒ Since 8² + 15² = 17², the base is a right-angled triangle.

Calculating Base Area and Perimeter:

⇒ Area of base = 1/2 × 8 × 15 = 60 cm²

⇒ Perimeter of base = 8 + 15 + 17 = 40 cm

Finding the Height (h) of the prism:

⇒ LSA = Perimeter × h

⇒ 480 = 40 × h

⇒ h = 480 ÷ 40 = 12 cm

Calculating the Volume:

⇒ Volume = Area of base × h

⇒ Volume = 60 × 12 = 720 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 720 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

questions.question: An unbiased dice is thrown. What is the probability of getting a multiple of 3?
questions.solution:
**Concept Used:**

Probaility = (Number of favorable outcomes)/(Sample space) 

**Calculation:**

The numbers which are multiples of 3 are 3 and 6. These two numbers appear on the faces of the dice. Therefore, there are 2 favorable outcomes.

The total number of possible outcomes is 6 because the dice has 6 faces.

Therefore, the probability of getting a multiple of 3 when an unbiased dice is thrown is:

Favorable outcomes / Total outcomes = 2 / 6 = 1 / 3

**∴ The probability of getting a multiple of 3 is 1/3.**

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__** As the question has asked about the passed student so, we will make the Venn diagram of passed student.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b2e5d8c30c8a86bf91ec5f728222a31a8a7f5d8abf4fdda2c7621253fdbd8bee.png] 

Let total student = 100%

Total passed student = 100 - 30 = 70

But, 65 + 58 = 123% passed

So, Passed in both subject = 123% - 70% = 53%

Passed in 1 subject = 12 + 5 = 17%

Passed in 1 subject = 17% of 2500 = 425

**∴ The correct answer is 425.**

**Given:**

35% failed in one subject

42% failed in other subjects

**Calculation:**

% failed in only one subject = 35% of 2500

⇒ 875

% failed in only other subject = 42% of 2500

⇒ 1050

% failed in both subject

⇒ 30% of 2500

⇒ 750

Passed in one subject = (875 - 750) + (1050 - 750)

⇒ 425

**∴ Number of students passed only in one subject = 125 + 300 = 425**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**

Given:

35% failed in one subject

42% failed in other subjects

Calculation:

% failed in only one subject = 35% - 30% = 5% 

% failed in only other subject = 42% - 30% = 12%

If someone fails in one subject, it means that he/she passed in the other one.

Thus, % of students who passed in only one subject = 5% + 12% = 17%

∴ Number of students who passed only one subject = 17/100 × 2500 = **425**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **__Confusion Points__**

You may think that the question should ask about the students who failed.

But the information asked in the question is apt.

If a student fails in only one subject, it also means that he is passed in one subject and failed in one. (as there are only 2 subjects)

**Thus, the no. of students who fail in only one subject will be equal to the no.of students who passed in only one subject.**

Therefore, the correct answer is **425**.

Assess the true nature of the relationship between event A and event B without any other assumptions and based only on the information given below.

**Event A: **I have been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes.

**Event B:** My doctor prescribed me medicines for type 2 diabetes.

options.text: Event A is the effect and event B is its immediate and major cause.
Event B is the effect and event A is its immediate and major cause.
Event A is an effect but event B is not its immediate and major cause.
Event B is an effect but event A is not its immediate and major cause.

questions.solution:
Event A: I have been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes.

Event B: My doctor prescribed me medicines for type 2 diabetes.

I have been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for which my doctor prescribed me medicines for type 2 diabetes.

Clearly, Event B is the effect of Event A.

Hence,** Event B is the effect and event A is its immediate and major cause**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**What are Causes?**

Causes are the conditions under which an event occurs.

For example, can you guess the causes for the following? 

The police increased security around the President's house.

Lots of people buy a particularly expensive brand of washing machines around Diwali. Easily, we can guess the causes for the above events. 

There were reports of threats against the President. 

There was a high discount or sale for that brand during Diwali.

**Sufficient & Necessary Conditions:**

In a cause and effect question, the cause is the sufficient condition. It is assumed that the sufficient condition of the occurrence of the events must include the different necessary conditions as well. 

A necessary condition is one that must be satisfied for the occurrence of an event. 

E.g. You must adhere to the deadline to get your work appraised. 

This means if you get your work appraised, you have to adhere to the deadline. Or; if you do not adhere to the deadline, you do not get your work appraised. 

A condition is called a sufficient condition if in a certain event, you are satisfied with the results.

E.g. Being human is a sufficient condition for being a mammal. The act of being a human is not possible unless one is also a mammal. But it is not necessary that being human is a necessary condition for being a mammal.

questions.question:
Which two signs and numbers should be interchanged to make the following equation correct?

16 × 18 + 2 - 14 ÷ 3 = 38
questions.solution:
1) 14 and 18, + and –

Given expression: 16 × 18 + 2 - 14 ÷ 3 = 38

After replacing the numbers and symbols, we get:

16 × 14 – 2 + 18 ÷ 3 = 38

=> 224 – 2 + 6 = 38

=> 230 – 2 = 38

=> 228 ≠ 38

2) 14 and 18, + and ×

Given expression: 16 × 18 + 2 - 14 ÷ 3 = 38

After replacing the numbers and symbols, we get:

16 + 14 × 2 - 18 ÷ 3 = 38

=> 16 + 28 – 6 = 38

=> 44 – 6 = 38

=> 38 = 38

3) 16 and 3, - and ÷

Given expression: 16 × 18 + 2 - 14 ÷ 3 = 38

After replacing the numbers and symbols, we get:

3 × 18 + 2 ÷ 14 - 16 = 38

=> 54 + 0.14 – 16 = 38

=> 54.15 – 16 = 38

=> 38.15 ≠ 38

4) 16 and 14, - and ×

Given expression: 16 × 18 + 2 - 14 ÷ 3 = 38

After replacing the numbers and symbols, we get:

14 - 18 + 2 × 16 ÷ 3 = 38

=> 14 – 18 + 10.67 = 38

=> 24.67 – 18 = 38

=> 6.67 ≠ 38

 Hence, ‘14 and 18, + and ×’ is the correct answer.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

• "The king gave a reward for bravery and loyalty." - This changes the verb from "rewarded" to "gave a reward."
 
• "For loyalty and bravery it is said that the king gave reward." - This option changes the entire sentence structure and meaning.

• Active Voice - **Who + verb + object.**

• Note - In sentences containing** 'who'**, the passive voice starts with **'by whom'**.

__

• Change object into subject.
 
• Change subject into object.
 
• Always use the third form of the verb in passive voice.
 
• Use 'by' before the new object.

 इसलिए, सही निष्क्रिय आवाज़ है *By whom is the guitar played in the museum. *

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are ***correct ***about Buddhist texts?

1. The Buddha’s teachings were included in the Abhidhamma Pitaka. 

2. The Vinaya Pitaka included rules and regulations for those who joined the sangha or monastic order.

3. The Sutta Pitaka dealt with philosophical matters.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2 only.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Buddha taught orally** through **discussion **and **debate**.
 
• **Men and women** attended these** discourses and discussed **what they heard.
 
• **None of the Buddha’s speeches was written** down during his **lifetime**.
 
• **After **his **death **(c. **fifth-fourth century BCE**) his teachings were **compiled **by his **disciples **at a **council of “elders” or senior monks **at **Vesali **(**Pali **for **Vaishali **in present-day **Bihar**).
 
• These compilations were known as **Tipitaka** literally,** three baskets to hold different types of texts**.
 
 
• They were first **transmitted orally** and then **written **and classified according to length as well as subject matter.
 
• The **Vinaya Pitaka** included** rules and regulations **for those **who joined the sangha or monastic order. **Hence, Statement 2 is correct.
 
• The **Buddha’s teachings** were included in the **Sutta Pitaka. **Hence, Statement 1 is incorrect.
 
• The **Abhidhamma Pitaka **dealt with **philosophical matters**. Hence, Statement 3 is incorrect.
 
 
 
• **Each Pitaka **comprised a number of **individual texts.**
 
• Later, **commentaries were written on these texts** by Buddhist scholars.
 
• As **Buddhism travelled to new regions** such as **Sri Lanka**, other texts such as the **Dipavamsa **(literally, the **chronicle of the island**) and **Mahavamsa **(the **great chronicle**) were **written**, containing **regional histories of Buddhism.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• When Buddhism spread to **East Asia**, pilgrims such as **Fa Xian and Xuan Zang** travelled all the way from China to India in search of texts.

 
 
• These they took back to their own country, where they were **translated **by scholars.
 
 
 
• **Indian Buddhist teachers** also **travelled **to **faraway places**, carrying texts to **disseminate the teachings of the Buddha**.
 
• Buddhist texts were **preserved in manuscripts **for several centuries in **monasteries **in **different parts of Asia**.
 
• **Modern translations **have been prepared from** Pali, Sanskrit, Chinese and Tibetan texts.**

__**Statement I: The process in which one plate slides beneath another plate is a zone of convergence.**__

__
 
• A subduction zone is the biggest crash scene on Earth.
 
• These boundaries mark the collision between two of the planet's tectonic plates.
 
• The plates are pieces of crust that slowly move across the planet's surface over millions of years. 
 
• **Where two tectonic plates meet at a subduction zone, one bends and slides underneath the other, curving down into the mantle. **(The mantle is the hotter layer under the crust.) **and the subduction area is known as the Benioff zone.**
 
• Tectonic plates can transport both continental crust and oceanic crust, or they may be made of only one kind of crust.
 
• Oceanic crust is denser than continental crust. At a subduction zone, the oceanic crust usually sinks into the mantle beneath lighter continental crust. 
 
• **Scientists first identified subduction zones in the 1960s, by locating earthquakes in the descending crust. Now, new instruments can precisely track the shifting tectonic plates.**
 
• **A dipping planar (flat) zone of earthquakes is produced by the interaction of a downgoing oceanic crustal plate with a continental plate.**

• The process of subduction is very common along the convergence boundary.
 
• Here the statement focussed on the process, not the situation.

**Statement II: Seafloor spreading becomes more prominent along the zone of convergences.**__

__
 
• Seafloor spreading occurs at divergent plate boundaries.
 
• As tectonic plates slowly move away from each other, heat from the mantle's convection currents makes the crust more plastic and less dense.
 
• The less-dense material rises, often forming a mountain or elevated area of the seafloor.
 
• The phenomenon is known today as plate tectonics.
 
• In locations where two plates move apart, at mid-ocean ridges, new seafloor is continually formed during seafloor spreading.**​**

• **One plate eventually slides beneath the other, a process known as subduction. The subduction zone can be defined by a plane where many earthquakes occur, called the Wadati–Benioff zone.**
 
• **A divergent boundary occurs when two tectonic plates move away from each other. Along these boundaries, earthquakes are common and magma (molten rock) rises from the Earth's mantle to the surface, solidifying to create a new oceanic crust. The Mid-Atlantic Ridge is an example of divergent plate boundaries**.

__
 
• The** Domain Name System (DNS)** is the** phonebook of the Internet**. Humans access information online through **domain names**, like testbook.com or espn.com. Web browsers interact through **Internet Protocol (IP) addresses**. DNS translates domain names to IP addresses so browsers can load Internet resources.
 
• Each device connected to the Internet has a **unique IP address **that other machines use to find the device. DNS servers **eliminate the need for humans** to memorize IP addresses such as **192.168.1.1 (in IPv4)**, or more complex newer **alphanumeric IP addresses** such as 2400:cb00:2048:1::c629:d7a2 (in IPv6).

• The process of **DNS resolution** involves **converting a hostname** (such as www.testbook.com) into a computer-friendly IP address (such as 104.20.37.240). An **IP address** is given to each **device on the Internet**, and that address is necessary to find the appropriate **Internet device** - like a street address is used to find a particular home. When a user wants to load a webpage, a **translation** must occur between what a user types into their **web browser** (testbook.com) and the **machine-friendly address** necessary to locate the testbook.com webpage.
 
• In order to understand the process behind the DNS resolution, it’s important to learn about the different **hardware components** a DNS query must pass between. questions.question: Which among the following generations of computer used the technology of transistors for the first time?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is the Second generation of computers used the technology of transistors for the first time.**

__
 
• The Second generation of computers (1956-1963) used transistors instead of vacuum tubes, which were used in the first generation of computers.
 
• Transistors were smaller, faster, and more reliable than vacuum tubes, and they consumed less power.
 
• The development of transistors was a major breakthrough in computer technology, as it allowed for the creation of smaller, faster, and more reliable computers.
 
• The second generation of computers also saw the introduction of magnetic core memory, which was faster and more reliable than the drum memory used in the first generation of computers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Third Generation: The third generation of computers (1964-1971) saw the introduction of integrated circuits, which were smaller and more reliable than transistors. Integrated circuits allowed for the creation of even smaller and faster computers, and they paved the way for the development of microprocessors.
 
• First Generation: The first generation of computers (1940s-1950s) used vacuum tubes as the primary electronic component. Vacuum tubes were large, fragile, and consumed a lot of power, and they were prone to failure. The first generation of computers were huge, expensive, and used mainly for scientific and military applications.
 
• Fourth Generation: The fourth generation of computers (1971-1989) saw the introduction of microprocessors, which were integrated circuits that contained all the components of a computer's central processing unit (CPU) on a single chip. Microprocessors were smaller, faster, and more energy-efficient than the previous generation of computers, and they led to the development of personal computers (PCs). The fourth generation of computers also saw the development of the graphical user interface (GUI) and the mouse, which made computers more user-friendly and accessible to non-technical users.

• Your deleted emails can be automatically removed from your trash folder permanently depending on your email provider or company's policies (often after 30 days).
 
• Check your Gmail inbox now. There is a list of folders on the left side of the screen (Inbox, Starred, Spam, etc). Your deleted emails will be located in a folder labeled "Trash" or "Bin" (the name of the folder depends on the user's language preferences).

Inbox:- a location on a computer where emails sent to you are stored.

Outbox:- Without an internet connection, users can read, reply to, and delete emails. All of your emails from the outbox are immediately sent whenever you're back online. Your emails might still be sitting in Gmail's outbox if you've been using this feature.

questions.question: Which among the following statements is incorrect about secondary memory?

options.text: It is known as the backup memory.
Data is permanently stored even if power is switched OFF.
Computer may run without the secondary memory.

questions.solution:
**Correct Answer: It is a volatile memory.**

__
 
• Secondary memory is also known as auxiliary memory or external memory.
 
• It is a type of computer memory that is used for long-term storage of data and programs, and it is not directly accessible to the CPU.
 
• Secondary memory is non-volatile, which means that data stored on it is not lost when the power is switched off.
 
• It is used for tasks such as storing operating systems, software applications, documents, media files, and other types of data that need to be accessed frequently but do not need to be kept in the primary memory (RAM) of the computer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• It is known as the backup memory: This statement is correct. Secondary memory is often used as a backup for data that is stored in primary memory (RAM).
 
• This is because the data stored in RAM is volatile and can be lost if the power is turned off or if there is a system crash.
 
• By contrast, data stored in secondary memory is non-volatile and can be retrieved even if the computer shuts down unexpectedly.
 
• Data is permanently stored even if power is switched OFF: This statement is correct.
 
• As mentioned earlier, secondary memory is non-volatile, which means that it retains data even when the power is switched off.
 
• This is in contrast to primary memory (RAM), which is volatile and loses its contents when the power is turned off.
 
• Computer may run without the secondary memory: This statement is also correct.
 
• While secondary memory is an important component of a computer system, a computer can still run without it.
 
• However, the absence of secondary memory will limit the amount of data and programs that the computer can store and access.
 
• The computer will have to rely solely on its primary memory (RAM), which is usually much smaller in capacity than secondary memory.
